claims.subject: H2/O2 copper chamber wall compatibility
claims.object: maximum wall mixture ratio 5 at average wall temperature 900 F (755 K), 2250 psia
claims.statement: Reliability studies indicated that for a H2/O2 copper chamber at 2250 psia a maximum wall mixture ratio of five at an average wall temperature of 900 F (755 K) was compatible.
qualifiers: Aerojet GG-cycle chamber context; compatibility (blanching/oxidation) criterion, not a structural allowable
claims.quote: a maximum wall mixture ratio of five at an average wall temperature of 900F (755 K) was compatable

claims.subject: coolant Mach number
claims.object: 0.35 to prevent sonic choking at bends, contractions and exit/entrance regions
claims.statement: To prevent sonic choking at bends, contractions or exit/entrance regions, coolant velocities were limited to a Mach number of 0.35; high-aspect-ratio (8) dual-width channels with surface roughness were selected.
qualifiers: former (Table 1) design; the present hot-channel criteria (Table 2) use aspect ratio 7
claims.quote: coolant velocities were limited t o a Mach number(Ma) of 0.35

claims.subject: hot-channel design criteria
claims.object: 10% heat-flux increase for streaks, 10% flow reduction for maldistribution, maximum depth/width 7, and a relatively high allowable gas-side wall temperature based on material yield-strength sensitivity
claims.statement: Aerojet's present hot-channel criteria account for injector streaking by a 10% increase in chamber heat flux and for flow maldistribution by a 10% reduction of channel flow, allow a maximum channel depth-to-width ratio of seven based on manufacturing, and set the allowable design gas-side wall temperature to a relatively high value based on the sensitivity of the material yield strength.
qualifiers: no numerical wall temperature in this text; Table 2 (PDF p.7) gives 1050 F, material dependent
claims.quote: The allowable design gas-side wall temperature is set to a relatively high value based on sensitivity of the material yield strength

claims.subject: former design film-cooling rule
claims.object: desired average wall temperature lower than 900 F
claims.statement: In the former design, the amount of film cooling was dictated by the desired average wall temperature (lower than 900 F).
claims.quote: The amount of film cooling added was dictated by the desired average wall temperature
